newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Consolidation seen as Belgian bourse hits a bump.
newsitem.headline: Consolidation seen as Belgian bourse hits a bump.

text.p: Belgian shares are expected to consolidate in the coming few days after falling in thin volume on profittaking on Monday following last week's rampant rally, traders said.
"There is no fundamental change in the market. People are simply taking profits," one trader said.
"Almost everything else is positive. Although interest rates are a bit higher, it is from a very low level," another trader noted.
Traders noted that individuals had been active, not just institutions, adding that the market remained well supported.
Two days ahead of Societe Generale de Belgique's 14,500 francs per share public offer on Tractebel, the latter turned out to be the busiest share by value on the Belgian bourse.
Plastics processor Deceuninck was one of the strongest performers of the day, rising 4.5 percent to 4,680 francs.
Traders said part of the strength was technical, although they noted that at more than 5,700 shares, the volume through the bourse was abnormally high.
Traders also noted that some of the cyclical stocks such as retailer Delhaize -- down 35 francs at 1,770 -- and steelmaker Cockerill Sambre -- down one franc at 131 -- were slipping.
The Bel-20 share index ended the day 16.19 points lower at 1,777.92, just below what some analysts had seen as rock solid support at 1,780.
However, traders were sanguine noting that overall volume was thin at just 1.5 billion francs.
